topic: Identical duplicate timestamps with identical values
scope: 6 blocks of 60 minutes on EU autumn switch Sundays 19:00-19:59 (2019-2023, 2025)
proposal: In a NEW derived dataset keep one row per timestamp and record the removed copy's source file and line numbers in a provenance table. If the reference comparison (B3) shows the real hour differs from the copy, also flag that hour 'dst_copy_suspect' and exclude it from feature/label windows.
rationale: The second copy is byte-identical and so adds no information; it is unknown whether it replaced a real hour
open_choice_for_owner: Keep-one-and-flag vs mask the hour entirely

proposal: Do not pick a variant by position. Default: set those 4 minutes to missing in the derived dataset with flag 'conflicting_duplicate' and keep both variants in the provenance table. A variant may be chosen only if a reference gives decisive, documented evidence (price similarity at minute level is weak, so require agreement of OHLC within half a typical spread for one variant only).
rationale: 4 Sunday-open minutes; masking costs little and avoids silent bias (the existing Parquet files silently kept the first occurrence)

proposal: Never fill, forward-fill or interpolate prices in the base M1 dataset. Keep a sparse index plus per-bar flags: gap_before_minutes, after_weekend, after_long_gap, in_closure (hypothesis category kept as metadata). Mask any feature window or label horizon that crosses a gap longer than a set limit. Resampled bars carry expected/observed minute counts and an 'incomplete' flag below a completeness threshold.
rationale: Filling would create fake returns and leak structure; masking keeps the data honest
depends_on: Timezone candidate (closure calendars depend on UTC mapping)
open_choice_for_owner: Gap limit for masking (e.g. 5 min); resample completeness threshold (e.g. 80%)

scope: 2023-02-01 to 2023-07-31 (634 unexplained gaps; about 42.5k missing bars)
proposal: Flag the period 'low_quality_2023' in the derived dataset. Exclude it from model training and evaluation metrics by default, and report a sensitivity analysis that includes it. Do not splice another vendor's data into the HistData base series (it mixes price type and vendor). Optionally compare against a fresh HistData download or the 2023 ZIP in ~/Downloads (read-only, with approval) to see whether HistData has republished the year.
rationale: Avoid biased statistics from a degraded period while keeping it auditable
open_choice_for_owner: Exclude vs include-with-flag; whether to check a fresh HistData download

proposal: Keep the 4 existing Parquet files as read-only legacy (they encode keep-first dedup and the naive source clock). After approval, write NEW versioned files under data/processed/ (e.g. eurusd_m1_v1.parquet) with: a tz-aware UTC index (or source clock if C6), the original source timestamp string, source file, line number, quality flags, and a manifest JSON (policy version, input SHA-256s, code version, row counts). Resample from the derived M1 with completeness counts; document bin alignment (UTC or 17:00 New York). Never overwrite; tests compare the regenerated files against raw inputs.
depends_on: Approval of the timezone candidate and P1-P4
open_choice_for_owner: Resample alignment: UTC midnight vs 17:00 New York session
